lessons.title: WebViewClient ignores SSL errors via proceed()
signals: onReceivedSslError calls handler.proceed() unconditionally
No handler.cancel() branch or certificate pinning check
lessons.why_exploitable: A network attacker presents any certificate and the WebView accepts it, so injected content or script runs in a JS-enabled WebView and can steal data.
false_positive_guards: Handler calls cancel() or validates against a pinned certificate
Code only exists in debug-only source sets
lessons.severity_guidance: High when the WebView has JS enabled or loads sensitive pages.

lessons.title: Exported component without permission reaches sensitive sink
signals: registerReceiver(<Receiver>, filter) without a permission argument or RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED
<service> exported=true with no android:permission
Intent extras flow to WebView, file upload or network sinks
lessons.why_exploitable: Any installed app can send broadcasts or start the service with crafted extras. The app then loads attacker URLs or uploads readable files to an attacker-chosen server.
false_positive_guards: Component protected by signature-level permission or RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED
Handler ignores extras or validates the caller and input
lessons.severity_guidance: Medium; high if extras reach file, WebView or upload sinks.

lessons.title: Hardcoded credentials with client-side authentication
signals: Username and password literals in code or resources
<Class> compares input against a local map or constant
lessons.why_exploitable: Decompiling the APK reveals the secrets. Local-only authentication lets anyone log in or bypass the check, and shared secrets may unlock backend access.
false_positive_guards: Literal is a non-secret placeholder or a test fixture excluded from release
Server verifies credentials and the local value is not a secret
lessons.severity_guidance: High when credentials grant real access or are shared across installs.

lessons.title: Exported activity copies attacker-supplied stream URI and filename
signals: Exported activity handles EXTRA_STREAM or intent data URI
Destination filename derived from URI or <String> unsanitised
Copy is written to external storage
lessons.why_exploitable: The attacker supplies a file or content URI the app can read, such as private files. The app copies it to world-readable storage, and a crafted name allows path traversal.
false_positive_guards: Filename sanitised and URI scheme or authority allow-listed
Output stays in app-private storage
lessons.severity_guidance: Medium; high if private files are exposed or arbitrary paths written.
lessons.abstract_example: Uri u = getIntent().getParcelableExtra(<extraKey>); copy(openInputStream(u), new File(extDir, u.getLastPathSegment()));

lessons.title: Debuggable build or backup enabled in manifest
signals: android:debuggable="true" in release manifest
android:allowBackup="true" with sensitive local data
lessons.why_exploitable: run-as, debugger attach or adb backup lets an attacker with device access read private data such as stored credentials and tokens.
false_positive_guards: Flag appears only in the debug build variant
Backup rules exclude sensitive data
lessons.severity_guidance: Medium; raises impact of any local storage finding.

lessons.title: Exported provider guarded only by normal-level permission
signals: Provider exported=true and query returns credentials or tokens
Custom permission declared with protectionLevel normal or none
lessons.why_exploitable: Normal-level permissions are granted to any app that declares them, so a malicious app can query the provider and read secrets.
false_positive_guards: Permission is signature level or provider is not exported
Returned data is non-sensitive
lessons.severity_guidance: High when credentials or personal data are returned.

lessons.title: WebView loads intent-supplied URL with JS and file access
signals: loadUrl takes getDataString or getStringExtra(<urlKey>) without validation
Activity exported or BROWSABLE, or reachable through redirection
setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs(true) or file access enabled
lessons.why_exploitable: Attacker-controlled URLs, including file://, run script in the app origin and can read private app files or exfiltrate data.
false_positive_guards: URL strictly validated against https host allow-list before loading
File access disabled and component unreachable by other apps
lessons.severity_guidance: High if exported and JS or file access enabled; medium if only reachable indirectly.

lessons.title: Deep link URL validation by weak string check
signals: Deep-link query param checked with endsWith or contains instead of host parsing
Another deep-link path loads the parameter with no check
lessons.why_exploitable: Substring checks pass for attacker URLs, such as evil host with allowed string in the query, and unchecked paths load anything, so attacker content loads in the WebView.
false_positive_guards: Uri.parse(<String>).getHost() compared by exact match with scheme enforced
Parameter is not loaded into a WebView or sensitive sink
lessons.severity_guidance: High when the WebView is JS-enabled or the deep link is BROWSABLE.

lessons.title: Credentials stored in plaintext SharedPreferences
signals: putString with password or token key into normal SharedPreferences
No Keystore or EncryptedSharedPreferences wrapping
lessons.why_exploitable: Unencrypted secrets can be read via backup, debuggable run-as, root, or other file-disclosure bugs in the app.
false_positive_guards: Value is encrypted with a Keystore-backed key
Stored value is non-sensitive
lessons.severity_guidance: Medium; higher with backup, debuggable or file-read bugs.

lessons.title: Sensitive data written to logcat
signals: Log call with password, token or <String> variable
Logging not stripped in release builds
lessons.why_exploitable: Logs are readable through adb, on debuggable builds, or by privileged tooling, exposing credentials to anyone with device access.
false_positive_guards: Release build removes logging via ProGuard or R8 assumenosideeffects
Logged value is non-sensitive
lessons.severity_guidance: Medium; low if logs are stripped in release.

lessons.title: Cleartext HTTP traffic permitted
signals: usesCleartextTraffic="true" in manifest
Base config permits cleartext globally
http:// endpoints or WebView loads
lessons.why_exploitable: Traffic over HTTP can be read or modified by a network attacker, enabling credential theft and content injection into WebViews.
false_positive_guards: Cleartext limited to localhost or specific dev domains
App uses only HTTPS endpoints
lessons.severity_guidance: Medium; high if sensitive data or WebView content uses HTTP.

lessons.title: Credentials sent in implicit broadcast
signals: sendBroadcast with action-only Intent carrying secret extras
No receiver permission argument or setPackage
lessons.why_exploitable: Any app can register a receiver for the action and read the secrets from the extras.
false_positive_guards: Intent restricted with setPackage or signature-level receiver permission
Extras contain no sensitive data
lessons.severity_guidance: Medium; high for passwords or tokens.

lessons.title: FileProvider paths expose root or private directories
signals: root-path path="/" or broad files-path in provider paths XML
grantUriPermissions="true" with attacker-influenced URI or intent
lessons.why_exploitable: A broad mapping lets any file, including private prefs and databases, be shared as a content URI. Combined with intent redirection, attackers obtain read grants.
false_positive_guards: Paths limited to a dedicated subdirectory of shared files
Provider not reachable by attacker-controlled intents
lessons.severity_guidance: High when combined with an intent-handling or grant-leaking component.

lessons.title: Intent redirection via attacker-supplied nested Intent
signals: Exported component extracts an Intent extra and passes it to startActivity
No check of target component or caller
lessons.why_exploitable: The app launches the attacker's Intent with its own identity, reaching non-exported components, using its permissions and granting URI access.
false_positive_guards: Nested intent resolved and restricted to an allow-listed component
Component not exported and extras come from trusted code
lessons.severity_guidance: High; enables access to internal components and private data.

guidance:
- L01 WebViewClient ignores SSL errors via proceed() (CWE-295, M5: Insecure Communication)
  Applies to: WebViewClient, Activity; APIs: onReceivedSslError, SslErrorHandler.proceed, WebViewClient
  Look for: onReceivedSslError calls handler.proceed() unconditionally; No handler.cancel() branch or certificate pinning check
  Why: A network attacker presents any certificate and the WebView accepts it, so injected content or script runs in a JS-enabled WebView and can steal data.
  Not a finding when: Handler calls cancel() or validates against a pinned certificate; Code only exists in debug-only source sets
  Severity: High when the WebView has JS enabled or loads sensitive pages.

- L02 Exported component without permission reaches sensitive sink (CWE-926, M8: Security Misconfiguration)
  Applies to: BroadcastReceiver, Service, Activity; APIs: registerReceiver, onReceive, android:exported, onStartCommand
  Look for: registerReceiver(<Receiver>, filter) without a permission argument or RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED; <service> exported=true with no android:permission; Intent extras flow to WebView, file upload or network sinks
  Why: Any installed app can send broadcasts or start the service with crafted extras. The app then loads attacker URLs or uploads readable files to an attacker-chosen server.
  Not a finding when: Component protected by signature-level permission or RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED; Handler ignores extras or validates the caller and input
  Severity: Medium; high if extras reach file, WebView or upload sinks.

- L03 Hardcoded credentials with client-side authentication (CWE-798, M1: Improper Credential Usage)
  Applies to: Activity, Util class; APIs: String.equals, HashMap.put, SharedPreferences
  Look for: Username and password literals in code or resources; <Class> compares input against a local map or constant
  Why: Decompiling the APK reveals the secrets. Local-only authentication lets anyone log in or bypass the check, and shared secrets may unlock backend access.
  Not a finding when: Literal is a non-secret placeholder or a test fixture excluded from release; Server verifies credentials and the local value is not a secret
  Severity: High when credentials grant real access or are shared across installs.
  Example: if (input.equals("<literalSecret>")) grantAccess();

- L04 Exported activity copies attacker-supplied stream URI and filename (CWE-22, M4: Insufficient Input/Output Validation)
  Applies to: Activity; APIs: getParcelableExtra, ContentResolver.openInputStream, Uri.getLastPathSegment, Environment.getExternalStorageDirectory
  Look for: Exported activity handles EXTRA_STREAM or intent data URI; Destination filename derived from URI or <String> unsanitised; Copy is written to external storage
  Why: The attacker supplies a file or content URI the app can read, such as private files. The app copies it to world-readable storage, and a crafted name allows path traversal.
  Not a finding when: Filename sanitised and URI scheme or authority allow-listed; Output stays in app-private storage
  Severity: Medium; high if private files are exposed or arbitrary paths written.
  Example: Uri u = getIntent().getParcelableExtra(<extraKey>); copy(openInputStream(u), new File(extDir, u.getLastPathSegment()));

- L05 Debuggable build or backup enabled in manifest (CWE-489, M8: Security Misconfiguration)
  Applies to: Application manifest; APIs: android:debuggable, android:allowBackup, run-as, adb backup
  Look for: android:debuggable="true" in release manifest; android:allowBackup="true" with sensitive local data
  Why: run-as, debugger attach or adb backup lets an attacker with device access read private data such as stored credentials and tokens.
  Not a finding when: Flag appears only in the debug build variant; Backup rules exclude sensitive data
  Severity: Medium; raises impact of any local storage finding.
  Example: <application android:debuggable="true" android:allowBackup="true">

- L06 Exported provider guarded only by normal-level permission (CWE-200, M8: Security Misconfiguration)
  Applies to: ContentProvider; APIs: ContentProvider.query, UriMatcher.addURI, android:readPermission, protectionLevel
  Look for: Provider exported=true and query returns credentials or tokens; Custom permission declared with protectionLevel normal or none
  Why: Normal-level permissions are granted to any app that declares them, so a malicious app can query the provider and read secrets.
  Not a finding when: Permission is signature level or provider is not exported; Returned data is non-sensitive
  Severity: High when credentials or personal data are returned.
  Example: <provider android:exported="true" android:readPermission="<normalPerm>"/> // query() returns <secret>

- L07 WebView loads intent-supplied URL with JS and file access (CWE-79, M4: Insufficient Input/Output Validation)
  Applies to: Activity, WebView; APIs: WebView.loadUrl, getDataString, setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs, setJavaScriptEnabled
  Look for: loadUrl takes getDataString or getStringExtra(<urlKey>) without validation; Activity exported or BROWSABLE, or reachable through redirection; setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs(true) or file access enabled
  Why: Attacker-controlled URLs, including file://, run script in the app origin and can read private app files or exfiltrate data.
  Not a finding when: URL strictly validated against https host allow-list before loading; File access disabled and component unreachable by other apps
  Severity: High if exported and JS or file access enabled; medium if only reachable indirectly.

- L08 Deep link URL validation by weak string check (CWE-20, M4: Insufficient Input/Output Validation)
  Applies to: Activity, Deep link; APIs: Uri.getQueryParameter, String.endsWith, String.contains, WebView.loadUrl
  Look for: Deep-link query param checked with endsWith or contains instead of host parsing; Another deep-link path loads the parameter with no check
  Why: Substring checks pass for attacker URLs, such as evil host with allowed string in the query, and unchecked paths load anything, so attacker content loads in the WebView.
  Not a finding when: Uri.parse(<String>).getHost() compared by exact match with scheme enforced; Parameter is not loaded into a WebView or sensitive sink
  Severity: High when the WebView is JS-enabled or the deep link is BROWSABLE.
  Example: if (uri.getQueryParameter(<param>).endsWith(<domain>)) webView.loadUrl(<<String>>);

- L09 Credentials stored in plaintext SharedPreferences (CWE-312, M9: Insecure Data Storage)
  Applies to: Storage helper, Activity; APIs: SharedPreferences.Editor.putString, getSharedPreferences, EncryptedSharedPreferences, Keystore
  Look for: putString with password or token key into normal SharedPreferences; No Keystore or EncryptedSharedPreferences wrapping
  Why: Unencrypted secrets can be read via backup, debuggable run-as, root, or other file-disclosure bugs in the app.
  Not a finding when: Value is encrypted with a Keystore-backed key; Stored value is non-sensitive
  Severity: Medium; higher with backup, debuggable or file-read bugs.
  Example: getSharedPreferences(<name>, MODE_PRIVATE).edit().putString(<prefsKey>, password).apply();

- L10 Sensitive data written to logcat (CWE-532, M9: Insecure Data Storage)
  Applies to: Activity, Any class; APIs: Log.d, Log.v, Log.i, System.out.println
  Look for: Log call with password, token or <String> variable; Logging not stripped in release builds
  Why: Logs are readable through adb, on debuggable builds, or by privileged tooling, exposing credentials to anyone with device access.
  Not a finding when: Release build removes logging via ProGuard or R8 assumenosideeffects; Logged value is non-sensitive
  Severity: Medium; low if logs are stripped in release.
  Example: Log.d(<tag>, password);

- L11 Cleartext HTTP traffic permitted (CWE-319, M5: Insecure Communication)
  Applies to: Application manifest, Network config; APIs: android:usesCleartextTraffic, network_security_config, cleartextTrafficPermitted, HttpURLConnection
  Look for: usesCleartextTraffic="true" in manifest; Base config permits cleartext globally; http:// endpoints or WebView loads
  Why: Traffic over HTTP can be read or modified by a network attacker, enabling credential theft and content injection into WebViews.
  Not a finding when: Cleartext limited to localhost or specific dev domains; App uses only HTTPS endpoints
  Severity: Medium; high if sensitive data or WebView content uses HTTP.

- L12 Credentials sent in implicit broadcast (CWE-927, M8: Security Misconfiguration)
  Applies to: Activity, Service; APIs: sendBroadcast, Intent.putExtra, setPackage, LocalBroadcastManager
  Look for: sendBroadcast with action-only Intent carrying secret extras; No receiver permission argument or setPackage
  Why: Any app can register a receiver for the action and read the secrets from the extras.
  Not a finding when: Intent restricted with setPackage or signature-level receiver permission; Extras contain no sensitive data
  Severity: Medium; high for passwords or tokens.

- L13 FileProvider paths expose root or private directories (CWE-22, M8: Security Misconfiguration)
  Applies to: FileProvider, XML resource; APIs: FileProvider.getUriForFile, root-path, android:grantUriPermissions, FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION
  Look for: root-path path="/" or broad files-path in provider paths XML; grantUriPermissions="true" with attacker-influenced URI or intent
  Why: A broad mapping lets any file, including private prefs and databases, be shared as a content URI. Combined with intent redirection, attackers obtain read grants.
  Not a finding when: Paths limited to a dedicated subdirectory of shared files; Provider not reachable by attacker-controlled intents
  Severity: High when combined with an intent-handling or grant-leaking component.

- L14 Intent redirection via attacker-supplied nested Intent (CWE-939, M8: Security Misconfiguration)
  Applies to: Activity, Service, BroadcastReceiver; APIs: getParcelableExtra, startActivity, startService, sendBroadcast
  Look for: Exported component extracts an Intent extra and passes it to startActivity; No check of target component or caller
  Why: The app launches the attacker's Intent with its own identity, reaching non-exported components, using its permissions and granting URI access.
  Not a finding when: Nested intent resolved and restricted to an allow-listed component; Component not exported and extras come from trusted code
  Severity: High; enables access to internal components and private data.
